image_description: A full-body side profile of a chestnut horse (sorrel) standing on a dirt surface. The horse has a reddish-brown coat, a flaxen mane and tail, and a prominent white blaze on its face with white socks on its lower legs. It is wearing a halter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with large expressive eyes and mobile ears.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head structure is anatomically correct for an equine, with visible ears and eyes in natural positions.
The neck shows clear musculature and a natural arch connecting to the withers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Athletic build with tall, lean proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horse displays a fit, athletic physique with well-defined withers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coat coloration with no black points.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the body is chestnut, the image clearly shows white markings (blaze and socks). Strictly speaking, 'uniform' implies no other colors, but genetically this is a sorrel/chestnut. However, visually it fails the 'uniform/no other colors' description due to the white markings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mane and tail are distinctly lighter (flaxen/blonde) than the red body coat, which is characteristic of many sorrels.
The torso depth and back line appear structurally sound and proportional.
The tail is long, attached correctly, and shows individual hair strands.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long slender legs with single hoof per foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All four legs are visible, slender, and terminate in single hooves. No extra limbs or fusion detected.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific breed/color classification (Sorrel/Chestnut) and rule out misclassification as a generic horse or other equine.
To verify the skeletal integrity of the legs and spine, ensuring no subtle warping or joint anomalies common in AI generations.
Hooves are high-risk areas for melting into the ground; need to verify sharp boundaries between hoof and dirt.
To check for texture consistency in the hair, looking for clumping or unnatural smoothing artifacts.
To ensure the background fence maintains linear perspective and does not warp around the subject.

focus_areas: Mane and tail texture for strand coherence
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the white socks on the legs. Ensure they don't look like 'painted on' textures but have proper volume. Check if the halter straps follow the curvature of the head correctly without clipping through the skin or fur.
